web_title: 7. Why the Price Is What It Is: Valuation, Reverse DCF & Peer Comps
book_title: What You Pay for the Toll Road: Reverse DCF, Senior Claims & De-Rating Math
question: At $1,069.43 per share, what does McKesson's valuation imply after deducting $15.22B of debt, opioid, NCI, and lease claims, and why does the reward-to-risk fall short of our 1.50:1 hurdle?

epigraph.quote: Price is what you pay; unencumbered enterprise claims and exit multiples decide what you keep.
epigraph.author: Institutional Valuation Desk Maxim

web_blocks.title: Current Valuation Snapshot & $15.22B Senior Claims Bridge

web_blocks.html: At the verified November 20, 2026 close of $1,069.43 (and $1,052.21 on the November 23 TradingView snapshot), McKesson carries a $121.48B to $123.51B equity market cap [24, 25]. On headline Finviz ratios, shares trade at 26.97x trailing GAAP earnings, 19.99x forward earnings, 16.33x EV/EBITDA, 17.04x price-to-free-cash-flow (P/FCF), and a 1.30x PEG ratio [25]. Management guides FY2027E Adjusted EPS to $45.60–$46.40 ($46.00 midpoint) [6, 8]. That puts the stock at 23.25x current-year adjusted earnings.

Headline enterprise value ($128.57B on Finviz) understates McKesson's true senior claims [25]. Per the Q2 FY2027 Form 10-Q (as of September 30, 2026), total debt rose to $9,208M ($3,234M in Med-Surg term loans) against $6,528M in cash [3]. Adding $5,163M in opioid litigation liabilities ($600M current plus $4,563M long-term), $2,563M in redeemable noncontrolling interests, and $1,953M in operating lease liabilities brings conservative debt-like claims to $15.22B ($5.55B net debt and commercial obligations + $5.16B opioid + $2.56B NCI + $1.95B leases) [3, 21].

Deducting $15.22B of senior claims from a conservative 8.5% WACC, 3.0% terminal-growth DCF on $5.80B normalized Free Cash Flow yields a Base fair value of $1,160.00 per share (versus Finviz consensus of $1,173.21) [2, 3, 25]. Notice how the 3.5%/yr share-count reduction assumption already nets out ~$684M/yr of opioid settlement cash outflows inside CFO/FCF [2]. If MSO put redemptions or PMG/Option Care integration cap annual buybacks at $3.5B instead of $4.8B, annual share shrinkage slows toward 2.5%.

web_blocks.the_number: $1,160.00 Base Fair Value ($1,113.00 Probability-Weighted Expected Value)
web_blocks.how_calculated: We run a 10-year DCF on $5.80B normalized FCF at 8.5% WACC and 3.0% terminal growth, then deduct $15.22B of senior claims ($5.55B net debt/obligations + $5.16B opioid + $2.56B NCI + $1.95B leases). We cross-check with 19.6x FY29E Adjusted EPS ($59.10) and probability-weight Bull ($1,350 at 20%), Base ($1,160 at 55%), and Bear ($820 at 25%).
web_blocks.the_inputs: FY2027E Adj. EPS guidance $45.60–$46.40 ($46.00 midpoint), Q2 FY2027 debt $9,208M, cash $6,528M, opioid claims $5,163M, redeemable NCI $2,563M, leases $1,953M, and ~3.5%/yr net buybacks (net of ~$684M/yr opioid cash outflows).
web_blocks.the_range: Bear $820.00 (16.5x stressed ~$49.70 EPS) | Base $1,160.00 | Bull $1,350.00 (24.5x ~$55.10 EPS). Finviz consensus target sits at $1,173.21.
web_blocks.if_off: Even at the $994.71 support zone low against the $865.85 stop, $1,160.00 yields only 1.28:1 R:R (<1.50:1 hurdle). At $1,069.43 CMP, R:R is 0.45:1 (0.51:1 on Finviz $1,173.21), forcing a REJECTED (VALUATION) verdict.

web_blocks.html: A segment-level Sum-of-the-Parts cross-check confirms why $1,160.00 is a fair Base ceiling. Core North American Pharmaceutical distribution generates roughly $3.8B in annual EBIT and warrants 12.0x to 13.0x EV/EBIT (~$47.5B EV) given 1.03% operating margins and CVS concentration [1, 2]. Oncology & Multispecialty (~$1.4B EBIT) plus RxTS (~$1.1B EBIT) command higher 18.0x to 20.0x specialty/tech multiples (~$47.5B EV) [2, 6]. Medical-Surgical / Wellverse (~$0.9B EBIT) adds ~$11.0B EV at 12.0x, aligning with Apollo's $1.25B minority valuation and $3.23B term loan [3, 9].

Adding McKesson's 49% proposed Option Care Health stake (~$1.4B) and corporate adjustments (~$1.5B) yields ~$149.0B gross enterprise value before senior claims [12]. Subtracting our $15.22B claims bridge ($5.55B net debt/obligations + $5.16B opioid + $2.56B NCI + $1.95B leases) leaves ~$133.8B in equity value, or ~$1,159 per share across 115.46M shares [3, 25]. Both our DCF ($1,160.00) and SOTP (~$1,159) converge well below the level needed to justify new capital.

Investors should also note the sensitivity of our $1,160.00 Base valuation to terminal-rate and margin assumptions. Each 50-basis-point increase in WACC (from 8.5% to 9.0%) lowers equity fair value by roughly $115 per share, pushing Base value down toward $1,045.00—below the November 20 close [3, 25]. Conversely, holding 8.0% WACC requires Oncology and RxTS to compound EBIT above 10.5% annually without IRA Part B or 340B fee compression [4, 20].

book_paragraphs: Valuation is where an admiring business story meets cold arithmetic. At the November 20, 2026 close of $1,069.43 (and $1,052.21 in the November 23 snapshot), McKesson commands nearly 20x forward earnings and 16.33x EV/EBITDA [24, 25]. Those multiples sit in the top quartile of its ten-year trading history, well above its five-year median of 16.5x to 18.0x forward earnings [16, 25].

To test what is priced in, we must account for every senior claim ahead of common shareholders. The Q2 FY2027 Form 10-Q shows $9,208 million of debt (including $3,234 million of Med-Surg term loans), $6,528 million of cash, $5,163 million of opioid litigation liabilities, $2,563 million of redeemable noncontrolling interests, and $1,953 million of operating leases [3]. Deducting $15.22 billion in conservative net debt and debt-like claims from our 8.5% WACC DCF produces a Base fair value of $1,160.00 per share—closely aligned with Finviz consensus at $1,173.21 [25].

That $1,160.00 fair value exposes the asymmetry problem. Against a structural invalidation stop at $865.85, buying at $1,069.43 risks $203.58 for $90.57 of upside—a 0.45-to-1 ratio (0.51-to-1 at Finviz's $1,173.21) [24, 25]. Even waiting for the $994.71 support zone low risks $128.86 for $165.29 of upside, or 1.28-to-1—still below our 1.50-to-1 institutional threshold.

Red-team stress testing reinforces this discipline. A routine multiple compression to the 17.25x five-year median on FY2028E Base EPS ($52.44) values McKesson at $904.59, while an 8.5% stressed EPS growth path yields $860.95 over 12 months. When even the support shelf fails 1.50:1 reward-to-risk, capital must step aside.

Let us walk through the valuation math step by step so every number is transparent. At the November 20, 2026 close of $1,069.43, McKesson's equity market capitalization stands near $123.51 billion, and on the November 23 snapshot at $1,052.21 it sits near $121.48 billion [24, 25]. Standard financial portals report an enterprise value around $128.57 billion because they subtract cash from financial debt and stop there [25].

Institutional underwriting cannot stop at headline financial debt. Inside McKesson's Q2 FY2027 Form 10-Q, three other large claims sit ahead of common shareholders [3]. First, remaining opioid litigation liabilities total $5,163 million ($600 million current plus $4,563 million long-term), draining roughly $684 million of cash every year [2, 3]. Second, redeemable noncontrolling interests jumped to $2,563 million—up from $943 million—reflecting physician MSO put options and Apollo's Wellverse stake [3]. Third, operating lease liabilities add another $1,953 million [3].

When we combine $5.55 billion of net debt and commercial obligations (including $3,234 million of Med-Surg term loans) with $5.16 billion of opioid liabilities, $2.56 billion of redeemable NCI, and $1.95 billion of leases, total senior claims equal $15.22 billion [3]. Deducting $15.22 billion from our 8.5% WACC, 3.0% terminal-growth DCF on $5.80 billion of normalized Free Cash Flow yields $1,160.00 per share. That sits within 1.1% of the Finviz analyst consensus target of $1,173.21 [25].

We also tested the Reverse DCF sensitivity to buybacks. In FY2026, McKesson repurchased $4.75 billion of stock, shrinking its share count by roughly 3.5% per year even after funding $684 million in annual opioid payments inside operating cash flow [2]. However, if physician MSO put redemptions or integration spending on the $2.25 billion Precision Medicine Group deal and $1.40 billion Option Care Health stake cap annual buybacks at $3.5 billion, share-count shrinkage slows toward 2.5% per year [3, 12, 13].

Finally, historical valuation bands warn against paying peak multiples here. Over the past five years, McKesson's median forward P/E sat between 16.5x and 18.0x (17.25x midpoint) [16, 25]. Today it trades near 19.99x forward earnings [25]. If multiples simply revert to 17.25x on FY2028E Base EPS of $52.44, the stock trades at $904.59—a 15.4% drop from $1,069.43. Under an 8.5% stressed EPS growth rate ($49.91 FY28E), 17.25x values the shares at $860.95. That is why even a pullback to $994.71 fails our 1.50:1 asymmetry rule.

To see how fragile the current multiple is, compare McKesson's valuation today against its own cycle history and its direct peers. During the 2018–2019 opioid and generic-deflation trough, McKesson traded at 9.5x to 11.0x forward earnings and 7.5x to 8.5x EV/EBITDA [16]. Over the subsequent five years, as opioid settlements crystallized and specialty oncology scaled, its median multiple settled into a 16.5x to 18.0x forward P/E band [16, 25].

Today, at 19.99x forward earnings and 16.33x EV/EBITDA, the market is pricing McKesson as if its specialty mix shift will face zero regulatory or execution friction [25]. Compare that to Cencora (COR) at 15.63x forward P/E and 12.35x EV/EBITDA, or Cardinal Health (CAH) at 18.93x forward P/E and 15.24x EV/EBITDA [26]. While McKesson's 76.71% ROIC and 1.69% operating margin are clearly superior to COR's 23.63% ROIC and CAH's 1.32% margin, a four-turn P/E premium leaves no cushion if growth decelerates [25, 26].

Our Sum-of-the-Parts model makes the same point from a different angle. Valuing Core North American Pharmaceutical at 12.5x EBIT ($47.5 billion), Oncology & Multispecialty plus RxTS at 19.0x combined EBIT ($47.5 billion), Medical-Surgical / Wellverse at 12.0x EBIT ($11.0 billion), and the 49% Option Care Health stake plus corporate items yields ~$149 billion of gross enterprise value [2, 6, 12]. Once we subtract $15.22 billion in senior claims—$5.55 billion net debt and commercial obligations, $5.16 billion opioid liabilities, $2.56 billion redeemable NCI, and $1.95 billion leases—common equity value lands at ~$133.8 billion, or ~$1,159 per share [3].

Notice how tightly our $1,160.00 DCF Base, ~$1,159 SOTP, and Finviz's $1,173.21 analyst consensus cluster together [25]. Three independent valuation methods all point to roughly $1,160–$1,173. That means the upside from $1,069.43 is less than 9%, while a simple mean-reversion to the 17.25x five-year median P/E on FY28E Base EPS ($52.44) implies $904.59 (-15.4%) [25]. Risking two dollars of downside to make one dollar of upside is not compounding; it is overpaying.

To appreciate why $15.22 billion in senior claims matters so much, consider how equity analysts often value McKesson on a simple P/E multiple. If you multiply $52.44 of FY2028E Adjusted EPS by 20x, you get $1,048.80, which looks roughly in line with the market [25]. If you multiply FY2029E Adjusted EPS of $59.10 by 20.3x, you get $1,200.00. That shortcut ignores two critical realities: first, whether the 20x multiple holds; and second, how much cash flow is spoken for before common shareholders get paid.

Every year, McKesson must service $9,208 million in gross debt, pay ~$684 million in opioid settlements until the $5,163 million liability is extinguished, honor $1,953 million in operating leases, and manage $2,563 million in redeemable noncontrolling interests tied to physician MSO puts and Apollo's Wellverse stake [2, 3]. Those obligations are not theoretical footnotes; they are real cash claims that compete directly with share buybacks and M&A.

In our Reverse DCF, we model $5.80 billion of normalized Free Cash Flow, which already reflects the ~$684 million annual opioid cash outflow inside operating cash flow [2]. At an 8.5% discount rate and 3.0% terminal growth, the market price of $1,069.43 implies 7.8% annual FCF compounding over ten years. Paired with 3.5% annual share shrinkage ($4.75 billion of FY2026 buybacks), that implies ~11.3% annual EPS growth [2, 6].

While McKesson's FY2027E Adjusted EPS guidance of $45.60 to $46.40 clears that hurdle, any slowdown in buybacks changes the equation [6, 8]. If MSO put redemptions or integration costs on Precision Medicine Group ($2.25 billion) and Option Care Health ($1.40 billion) force annual repurchases down from $4.8 billion toward $3.5 billion, EPS growth decelerates by roughly 100 basis points a year [3, 12, 13].

Even more important is multiple sensitivity. Across 2018–2025, McKesson's five-year median forward P/E sat at 16.5x to 18.0x [16, 25]. If broad market distribution pulls MCK back to 17.25x on FY2028E Base EPS ($52.44), the stock trades at $904.59. On an 8.5% stressed EPS growth path ($49.91 FY28E), 17.25x yields $860.95. That is why $1,160.00 is an honest Base ceiling and why paying $1,069.43—or even $994.71—lacks margin of safety.

Notice also how the market treats healthcare distributors differently when policy headlines hit. Between 2017 and 2020, McKesson's GAAP gross margin compressed from 5.7% to the mid-3% range as generic price deflation and branded mix shifted [2]. Today, GLP-1 volume (+26% YoY to $16 billion per quarter) drives similar gross margin dilution to 3.49%–3.61%, forcing Oncology and RxTS to carry consolidated profit growth [2, 8, 25].

If IRA Medicare Part B price negotiations (effective 2028) or 340B rebate model disputes compress oncology add-on fees by even 50 to 100 basis points, McKesson's ability to defend a 20x forward multiple disappears quickly [4, 20]. Deducting $15.22 billion in senior claims leaves $1,160.00 as a realistic Base fair value, not a conservative floor [3].

One final check on capital efficiency underscores the valuation tension. McKesson's headline 76.71% ROIC looks extraordinary partly because its -$3,954 million stockholders' deficit and -$7.78 billion net trade working capital shrink accounting invested capital [2, 3, 25]. While that negative working capital engine is genuine supplier float with zero receivables factoring, investors still pay 19.99x forward earnings and 17.04x free cash flow for an underlying distribution business whose GAAP operating margin is 1.54% [2, 25].

Ultimately, valuation is a discipline of patience. When three independent methods—our $1,160.00 DCF Base, our ~$1,159 SOTP, and Finviz's $1,173.21 consensus—cluster within 1.1% of each other, there is no hidden discount waiting to be unlocked at $1,069.43 [25].

When senior claims of $15.22 billion, top-quartile valuation multiples, and potential mid-cycle P/E compression to 17.25x ($904.59 on FY2028E Base EPS) are weighed honestly, the margin of safety required for new capital is simply absent at current market prices.
